source.title: Scaling Properties of Same-Family On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Yun-Tai Bao; Qin-Feng Li; Guo-qing Jiang; Li-Wei Chen; Zhi-Heng Qin; Xuan-Ping Li; Wenqiang Zhang; Xu-Hong Zhang

page_placements.theme: Training dynamics: early student gains, then regression as the student fits supervisor errors or over-optimises the teacher's signal

record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-to-strong transfer on math reasoning, but uses on-policy token-level distillation from student rollouts rather than the original weak-label fine-tuning recipe and does not report PGR.
record.gate_note: The study's own OPD and supervision-condition results are included. Results cited from Burns et al. and other studies are not rows. The paper reports peak accuracy, not PGR; the text says every observed weak-to-strong peak exceeds its teacher's score. It also reports aggregate comparisons between OPD objectives and describes post-peak proxy/gold dynamics.
record.test_reason: The study trains larger Qwen2.5 students under smaller RL-trained math experts, using on-policy distillation rather than weak-label fine-tuning. It reports whether student peaks exceed the teacher (V1), how outcomes scale with student size, teacher size and teacher score (V3), and how training changes (Delta-OPD, off-policy cold start, bootstrapping) alter transfer (V2). It does not compute PGR.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right; add four points. Peak gold score improves with teacher scale only up to about the student's scale. At a matched teacher score, smaller teachers transfer better. Pure off-policy distillation underperforms OPD. Direct RL on the student remains above every weak-teacher variant, so the appeal is amortizing one expert across sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses on-policy token-level teacher supervision on student-generated rollouts, after RL-trained Qwen2.5 math experts; the original claim concerns fine-tuning on weak-model-produced labels. Reports peak gold accuracy and scaling laws, not PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with teacher and student scale, OPD objective, and degree of on-policy supervision. Larger teachers do not always improve peaks for smaller students; Delta-OPD's advantage is not universal. Cold-start harm grows with the weak-to-strong capability gap.

fits_no_version.finding: After the gold-score peak, the teacher-induced proxy reward keeps rising wherever gold accuracy regresses; the smallest teacher shows the clearest regression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In weak-to-strong OPD, late-stage gold regression reflects overoptimization of the teacher's implicit reward.

fits_no_version.finding: Early OPD gold score rises linearly in the square root of token-mean reverse KL (R² 0.93–0.99 over 25 runs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-to-strong distillation has a regular initial transfer regime that is linear in square-root KL.

record.problems: One run per configuration, no repeated seeds, and no prompt-bootstrap intervals for aggregate accuracy. Evidence is limited to one model family and one math-reasoning mixture. PGR is not calculated; confidence intervals for scaling fits measure variation across cells, not training-seed uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-bearing outcome rows omitted. Cited findings from prior studies are excluded.

untested.parts: PGR is not computed. The original weak-label fine-tuning recipe is not tested as a main condition. Only math reasoning in Qwen2.5 is covered, not NLP classification, chess or reward modelling.
Auxiliary confidence loss and ensembling of weak supervisors are not tested. Effects are measured as peak gain, not PGR.
Only one model family and one math task. No representation-based predictors (e.g. linear probes).
Entire version: no distribution shift, no error-overlap analysis, no test of exploiting cases the supervisor cannot check.
Entire version: the appendix D local-KL derivation explains linear early transfer, not conditions under which the student must beat its supervisor.
Entire version: no vision or other modality.

missing.what: Per-teacher gold scores, needed as baselines for all weak-to-strong cells and for any PGR estimate. Available: 0.5B 39.8, 1.5B 63.6, 3B 73.6; 7B/14B only via direct-RL endpoints.
Intermediate-teacher validation: a 3B checkpoint scoring 66.0 teaches the 7B student to 73.8, below the 1.5B teacher (63.6) giving 77.5.

Pure OffPD and cold-start-only peaks relative to the teacher. OffPD trails OPD by 28.4 points in the extreme weak-to-strong cell and by under 1 point in same-base cells; cold start pins students near the teacher's score.
Direct RL on each student stays above every weak-teacher variant, so transfer is incomplete (PGR below 1).
Direct Delta-OPD peaks from the 0.5B teacher (65.3, 75.0, 79.9 at 3B, 7B, 14B) and per-pair gains.

record.verdict_notes: Single seed per configuration; one model family and one task. The recipe differs from Burns et al.: on-policy token-level distillation from RL experts, not fine-tuning on weak labels. Same-base and strong-to-weak cells are relinked to none. The law fits include them, but with teacher size capped at student size.

versions.untested_parts: Does not calculate PGR or test the original off-policy weak-label fine-tuning recipe; tests on-policy distillation on math reasoning.
Tests Vanilla-OPD versus Delta-OPD, not auxiliary confidence loss or ensembling weak supervisors; does not report PGR.
Only Qwen2.5 scales and a mixed GSM8K/MATH task are tested. No other task families, modalities, or representation predictors are tested.
No distribution-shift evaluation, comparison of weak/strong error overlap, or direct test of exploiting supervisor-uncheckable cases.
The local-geometry result explains initial transfer under a positive gradient-alignment condition; it does not derive conditions requiring a student to beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language modality.
